announcements.title: Cheat Sheet, App Update, Assignment 1 Reminder, and Help Sessions
announcements.message:
Dear All,

Four things this week:

1) Markdown cheat sheet. A one-page guide to writing mathematics in Markdown has been posted in the LMS, in the Assessments folder. You can also open it in SciQuant under Course Overview → References → Markdown & LaTeX Cheatsheet (once your app has synced content), or go straight to it here:
https://ahailu95.github.io/scie1500-content/Markdown_LaTeX_Cheatsheet.html

2) Updated app released. Version 2.2.0 went out last night. It fixes the code snippets navigation problem on devices without a trackpad, corrects a number of smaller issues, and adds clear reminders to switch away from the default Demo Mode tutor. See the separate update notice for the full list and download instructions.

3) Assignment 1 — do not use AI to answer the questions. Our markers have flagged a number of Batch 1 triweekly worksheet submissions for follow-up where AI use appears likely. Assignment 1 is due 26 August and the same expectations apply: the work you submit must be your own. Use the AI tutor to understand a concept, not to produce your answers.

4) Please come to a help session if you are stuck. Attendance at the last four sessions was zero. Two remain:
• Monday 24 August, 3:15–3:45 pm
• Wednesday 26 August, 3:15–3:45 pm
Meeting Room RM-401.G007-CEEP, Building 401 (Ground Floor), directly in front of the Barry J. Marshall Science Library.
Note that Wednesday falls on the Assignment 1 due date, so Monday is the last practical chance to get help before you submit.

Kind regards,
Atakelty (Unit Coordinator)

announcements.title: App Update v2.2.0 Available — Check Your AI Tutor, Plus Code Snippet and Lab Notebook Fixes
announcements.message:
A new version of SciQuant Assistant (v2.2.0) is now available for download from the LMS, in the SciQuant folder.

Most important — check which AI tutor you are using:
Some of you have been studying in Demo Mode without realising it. Demo Mode replies with a small set of canned sample answers: it cannot answer your own questions and knows nothing about your work. Go to Settings → AI Backend and check what is listed under "Current Backend". If it says Demo Mode, switch to SciQuant Cloud (the address is in the SciQuant folder in the LMS — it ends with workers.dev) or to Claude API with your own key. From this version on, the app shows a warning while Demo Mode is active, and first-time setup asks you to choose properly.

What else is included:
• Code snippets: you can now reach every week. Previously, on a laptop with a mouse rather than a trackpad, the week chips along the top could not be scrolled, so Week 3 onwards was unreachable. There are now arrow buttons and a scrollbar, and the mouse wheel works.
• Week 6 code snippets: the twelve snippet titles showed as "Untitled" and now show their real names (Setup and Imports, Definite Integrals, Area Between Two Curves, and so on).
• Lab notebooks corrected in Weeks 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 12 — mostly wording and worksheet part labels. The Week 2 Lab B cost comparison also had a genuine bug: if the threshold year fell beyond the 150-year horizon it produced a negative cost and saving. That is fixed. These corrections are already live in Colab, so "Open in Colab" gives you the corrected notebook even before you update.
• Setting up SciQuant Cloud is clearer: the app tells you where to find the address and warns you if you paste the LMS page address by mistake.
• First-time setup now asks for your lab session, so cohort-level usage trends are accurate. As always, this is never tied to your name or student number, and you can turn analytics off in Settings → Privacy & Data.

Week 5 lecture recordings are also now split into three shorter parts, which you will see without updating.

Not sure which version you're on? Check Settings → About in the app.

announcements.title: App Update v2.1.24 Available — Claude AI Fixes + Cohort Usage Analytics
announcements.message:
A new version of SciQuant Assistant (v2.1.24) is now available for download from the LMS, in the SciQuant folder.

What's included:
• Continued fixes for Claude AI tutoring reliability issues some of you may have experienced.
• New: the app can now collect anonymised, cohort-level usage data (e.g. how many students in a lab session have viewed lessons or attempted practice questions in a given week) — never anything tied to your name or student number.

To make the cohort data accurate, please go to Settings → Learning and select your lab session under "My Lab Session" after updating. This is optional — you can turn it off entirely in Settings → Privacy & Data → Usage Analytics.

Not sure which version you're on? Check Settings → About in the app.

announcements.title: Assignment 1 Released — Due 26 August
announcements.message:
Assignment 1 has been released. Due date is 26 August, as shown in the unit outline.

You can access the assignment file (a Jupyter Notebook) by clicking the Assignment 1 button under Assessments in the LMS. All instructions are inside that notebook — there's no need for separate Word or PDF files. You start and finish your assignment work inside the notebook.

The notebook has also been emailed to you as an attachment. If you'd like to work on it in Google Colab, forward that email to your Gmail account, then download the attachment from Gmail straight into your Google Drive — from there you can open it directly in Colab.

Post any questions in the discussion board. If you need help, let your lab instructors know, or come to the August help sessions on Monday and Wednesday afternoons — including today.

announcements.title: AI Tutor Access — Claude API Key or SciQuant Cloud
announcements.message:
There are two ways to get high-quality AI tutoring inside SciQuant this semester.

1. Your own Claude API key (recommended for the full semester)
You are encouraged to get your own personal Claude API key and use Claude as your tutor inside SciQuant. Sign up at console.anthropic.com, then go to Settings → Billing to add credit (a card or similar payment method is required). About $5–10 of credit is typically enough for a full semester of regular use. Full setup steps are in the app under Settings → AI Backend → Claude API.

2. SciQuant Cloud AI service (free, unit-provided)
If you'd rather not set up your own key, you can use the SciQuant Cloud AI service instead — during the first couple of weeks of semester, and during lab sessions for the rest of the semester. In the app, go to Settings → AI Backend → SciQuant Cloud and enter the Server URL. The Server URL is posted on the LMS — see the announcement there for the exact address, then leave the Auth Token field blank.

Please keep this URL to yourself — don't post it publicly or share it outside this unit. The cost of the service depends on how much it is used, so unnecessary sharing could affect availability for everyone in the class.

announcements.title: Welcome to SCIE1500 — Semester 2, 2026
announcements.message:
My name is Atakelty Hailu, and I'm excited to guide you through this unit.

• Teaching begins Monday 20 July. Please read the unit outline in full before Week 1.
• Download and install the SciQuant Assistant app — the link is in the LMS. All lessons, practice questions, and lab notebooks are delivered through the app.
• All assignment submissions and grading remain on the LMS.

What is new this semester:

The lab programme has been redesigned around Problem Briefs — realistic scientific scenarios you work on in permanent groups of 5–7. Each week your group submits a completed worksheet, but uploads are batched: worksheets are due in four batches (not weekly), on 11 Aug, 8 Sep, 29 Sep, and 27 Oct (all at 11:59pm). Every student must upload their own copy to LMS by the relevant batch deadline.

From Weeks 3 to 9, two groups present the previous week's work at the start of each lab (10 min, all members speak). Each group presents exactly twice. The final three labs (Weeks 10–12) replace the standard format with structured exam preparation: a mock exam workshop, a peer review exchange, and a gallery walk capstone.

The lectures are also new: science and mathematics content is now delivered as a single integrated set of lessons inside the SciQuant app.

Welcome — I look forward to working with you this semester.
Atakelty (Unit Coordinator)
